about: Agent workload (build.py data.workload, src/model.js agent*, node report.js --workload, the page's Agents tab). agentPlan uses turn_model and agentTurnPredict. Primary output is turns per agent-minute. Each turn reads trace growth plus the server's prefix re-read, decodes the model's observed or recorded answer length, then waits its tool gap. Output length and prefix re-read are inputs, not predictions. The old agentThroughput fields remain server-bound diagnostics without tool gaps. Synthetic short-prompt runs measure decode capacity, not agent throughput. Every numeric input carries {v, tag, src}.

v.src: INFERRED gain on a MEASURED decomposition: lab notes, prefill phase timing on the 16-agent replay control's engine log (75 reads over 512 tokens): a read costs ~1007 ms + 0.791 ms a token. Of the fixed part: parking the previous conversation 99 ms a read; giving the slot back 122 ms in 55 of the 75 reads (~83 ms a read); the batched read itself 614 ms + 0.8 ms a token; the remainder ~175 ms is INFERRED (checkpoint saves per stage and the 4-token header window). Copying the conversation into the slot takes another ~216 ms a read outside the read timing. The gain (halving the fixed part) is arithmetic, not yet measured

v.src: MEASURED: two paired 16-agent real-agent replays on odie (2x B70, Flash-Next, one build, 600 s each). Run 1: shared prefix 39.46 agent tok/s and 0.845 turns per agent-minute against the control's 33.4 / 0.769 (ledger rows odie-fnx-iq3xxs-2xb70-real-sp-n16-1026, odie-fnx-iq3xxs-2xb70-real-ctl-n16-1026). Repeat: 40.46 / 0.896 against 37.25 / 0.845 (odie-fnx-iq3xxs-2xb70-real-sp-r2-n16-1026, odie-fnx-iq3xxs-2xb70-real-ctl-r2-n16-1026). Two-run means: agent tok/s +13 %, turns per agent-minute +8 %. The gain range is the agent tok/s ratio of each pair (x1.18, x1.09); replay noise between the two identical control runs was ~11 % in agent tok/s (settings.replay_noise_pct), so the repeat's +8.6 % alone is inside noise and the mean +13 % only just outside it. The lever lowers fresh prompt tokens per output (F 18.8 and 18.6 against 23.95 and 19.8) rather than raising the prefill rate P; the report applies the measured agent tok/s ratio as a factor on P, which moves the ceiling P / F by the same ratio

prefill_pass.about: First-principles prefill (src/model.js prefillPass): a read of T fresh tokens runs in chunks of C tokens; each chunk makes one pass over the experts (almost every expert of every MoE layer is routed to when C x k >> E): the experts a card does not hold cross the PCIe link (less the share the CPU computes), the ones it holds are read once from VRAM. t(T) = ceil(T / C) x t_pass + T x m, t_pass = sum over the stages of nonresident bytes x (1 - cpu_share) / link + resident bytes / VRAM bandwidth, m = 2 x active params / (eta x card int8 ops). eta is the ONE fitted factor per engine (fit rows below); every other input is MEASURED, READ or INFERRED here. Attention and DeltaNet terms that grow with depth are left out (the model under-predicts the time of very long reads). P over an agent workload = mean read / (chunks per read x t_pass + mean read x m), over the read-size mix.

turn_model.about: Per-turn agent model (src/model.js agentReplaySim, agentTurnPredict; report.js --accuracy 'agent turn model'). A turn of one agent alone takes out / D1 + fresh / P, then the agent waits its recorded tool gap (x gap_scale) plus the client overhead before it sends the next turn. fresh = the trace's ideal fresh tokens of the turn (cold first prompt, else the prompt growth) x the serving model's tokenizer ratio + the server's re-read tokens per turn (its prefix reuse, servers below). out = the recorded output x the serving model's out_vs_recorded (a measured replay of that model, else the recording's own lengths). Many agents share one server: each running turn costs w = out / Dn + fresh / P server-seconds (an engine whose reads stall decode; else max of the two), and when the running turns' demand passes one server-second a second all of them slow by the same factor (fluid processor sharing). The replay's own counting follows: turns sent after the warm-up and done inside the window. Primary output: turns per agent-minute; useful tok/s = turns x each turn's output. Every input carries its tag and the runs it came from, so a score can hold out the run it scores
